title: Cat Goes Fishing
text: Unsurprisingly you are a cat and you are fishing: you'll start from the bank and slowly buy upgrades, new poles and even boats with the money you get from selling fish you catch. Cat Goes Fishing is a pretty charming game with a cute premise, decent gameplay and a good amount of stuff to do: sadly it can get repetitive fast and its progression is a tad too slow. -while very simple the graphics sport a charming art style -good amount of different fish to catch -quite many upgrades, things to buy and hats providing bonuses to be fished out of the water -two different game modes, one being more laid back while the other features a breakable line -simple music gets repetitive quite fast -quests can't be abandoned, thus if you get one requiring a fish you can't/ aren't able to catch you're going to get stuck for a possibly long time -gameplay can get frustrating, even with upgrades having to cast in the right place, wiggling your lure between useless fish, hoping the right one will be hooked and that no other fish will take a bite while you reel it in can be challenging: having to do so several times and failing will teste your nerves and ruin the relaxing atmosphere the game wants to create -unlocks eventually get too pricey, requiring lots of grinding -no way to save and exchange hats, you can only equip one and have to sell those you don't wish to keep -some things aren't explained, for example what the different fishing pole stats actually do Cat Goes Fishing is a decent game overall, I had fun for a few hours trying to catch fish, getting a nice hat, unlocking stuff and then trying to get a shark eat my bait: it's charming, has novelty value and can easily make you go "just one more fish before I quit". Sadly all this eventually grinds to a halt when you realize that the high end upgrades are very pricey, we're talking about a range from 250k to 320k when many big fishes can be sold for 7k: add to this the fact that you'll often have to also buy one time bonuses (rockets to go deeper, bombs to scare away the first fish that bites etc) not to mention having to rebuy upgrades for each new pole and you'll see how this can eventually get tiring. I was a bit torn overall but ultimately decided for a thumbs up due to the fact I had some decent fun with it and the game will do the same for you  for at least a few hours provided you don't mind its shortcomings, just don't be surprised when it loses its charm: if you're interested I'd get it on sale.

The skeleton of something that could have been better. It doesnt seem to be finished. As of late, there's a new contender in the rogue-like universe: Dead Cells. And Dead Cells is this opposite of Caveblazers. It's fun, it has an identity, the ennemies are not some generical monster you have seen a thousand times already. And it still pretty hard (at least before the last update). I do not recommend caveblazers. If you want a nice rogue like, then play Dead Cells (very promising), play Rogue Legacy, play Spelunky. But dont play Caveblazers.

text: Caveblazers is a side-scrolling, rogue-like, action adventure game where you explore randomly-generated cave systems, gain money and loot, and battle enemies and bosses. title: Caveblazers
text: If you enjoy difficult games - caveblazers is a perfect candidate for your library. The first hour is pretty repetitive, but it gets much better after that. In caveblazers, you venture down the cavern to explore it. It’s a roguelite platformer, where you’ll have to jump from wall to wall, fight different enemies and descend deep down into the cave. The game is aimed at hardcore roguelite/action/platformer audiences due to high difficulty. The combat system is pretty simple, but really well done. You have a melee weapon, a bow with unlimited ammo and a slot for special item. You just need to attack the enemy either from a distance or swing at him after he swings at you (and hopefully misses). If you swing at enemy at the same time he does – the swing is parried. Enemies do not have bounding boxes, so you can often go through them, thus flanking them and making them miss an attack against you. As you progress, you find new weapons and magic items that can give you one special ability like super speed, high jump or some passive perks. The variety is good and it leaves a lot of space to decision making: do I want to equip a boots that will allow me to run faster once in a while or do I want a demon that duplicates ranged attacks? You’ll spend lots of game time jumping, and this aspect is done really well too. Your character can jump from the walls, meaning that you can climb up this way. The jump controls are really well done, they are intuitive; you can change your direction mid-air, ensuring that you can easily navigate wherever you want to. AI deserves extra mention: monsters know how to jump from walls to walls and can find how to get to you. You also encounter friendly adventurers on your travel, and friendly ai really gives a great impression: it can maneuver carefully and traverse complicated levels while following you. The graphics are also nicely done and well-polished. The pixel art is done with love and fits the style of the game. •	The game often feels like it is relying on random too much. Some runs will be successful simply because your rooms spawned perfectly. •	I’ve also noticed that sometimes enemy-containing rooms are generated without open passages to them. You’d need to blow up the ground if you want to get to the enemies. There were no problems with the exit. •	At the rate the new perks are unlocked – the game gets a bit monotonous. Unless you unlock relevant perks – you always start with the same weapons. I’ve played for about 3 hours and I still only have one perk that gives me different ranged weapon. Caveblazers is the game that leaves a somewhat bad impression at first. During the first hour of playing, I seriously disliked how things went. The gameplay was really repetitive: spawn, die, repeat. After that time, I’ve unlocked a few perks that altered the gameplay process and the game began to feel different and more varying. I’m glad I’ve persevered past the first 1.5 hours, because after that the game really became fun. To sum it up, Caveblazers is very focused on its mechanics, so I’m pretty sure that you are new to the genre – it won’t motivate you to carry on. For those hardcore fans that enjoy this type of games and have some sort of idea about what they are getting into – I recommend the game.

title: Caveblazers
text: :  I feel like my purchase is already worth the fun I've had with this one. Tight controls!  Melee combat reminds me of Rouge Legacy.  Level design reminds me of Spelunky (especially the appearance of the first few levels and the top-to-bottom progression for each level). Earned XP feeds into the next unlock, but as far as I can tell, those are mostly aesthetic.  That makes it pretty fun, because all the little pieces of the hero are modular (head, hair, beard, hair color, shirt, pants... I think).  I've progressed through 3 different whole outfits in my hour so far. Tutorial is smoothly built into the first playthrough, which was very non-intrusive and appreciated.  Little cinematics are injected as you break through point thresholds and die.  Seems like characters will be showing up to build the suface area up (not unlike Rogue Legacy, but probaby an auto-build progression). Pickups are well done, like Binding of Isaac, (but with an inventory) with lots of different types of all the different categories; all of which can have very different effects on how the hero handles. One nice realization is that I don't play this game like Spelunky.  Since I had connected the two, I was rushing through levels.  Now I see it's nice to explore as much of a room as possible, trying to work my way back up, and over to goodies I would have otherwise missed.  Every powerup/pickup could be a legendary artifact, so it's SO worth scowering the levels as much as possible. On the down-side, I've realized my limits in skill, and hope that I haven't hit a wall already, as a result.  I'm not very good at shooting, so I've been practicing.  My melee skill is usually just button mashing, with an occasional dive stab.  As a result of both, unlike the narrator of the trailer, I have not beat a boss yet, after replaying various iterations of the first 2 levels over and over (20 times?).  So far, my unlocked perks (select one to have a different sort of build) are offset by weaknesses, so I'm not sure that "grinding" will really make me better (like how Rogue Legacy works)... I actually have to get better if I'm going to feel like I'm making progress.  It's also likely, however, that I'll get a sweet combination of goodies and "buffs" on a given run; where I luck out as more powerful than on the average run, and forge ahead that way. One realized feature that I have to praise is how (some?) humanoid enemies pick up and use items!  This not only adds a delicious dose of realistic interaction, but dropping an unknown potion for an orc to test for you is a safer way to learn what random affect it has;  at the risk that it'll make them overpowered, but also at the risk they'll cath on fire, not you.

title: Caveblazers
text: UPDATED REVIEW, 2017 ~ This game has come almost full circle from the first time I reviewed it - customization options, better sprites, more pizazz and humor and life(even just the Simlish that the monsters and characters speak is a highly welcome addition), a severely increased amount of loot and treasure and generally just THINGS TO DO. I still take issue at the 8 directional firing bow, but with such a plethora of options as you plod through the caves, in terms of weaponry or weird items, that salty feeling is quickly negated.  There seems to still be a slight hit box issue, but it doesn't seem to matter as much because the motion of your character is fluid enough to where it feels meaningful even on a miss(which is stellar game design).  Before, where I would gripe that killing monsters isn't worth your time because they don't drop loot, there's enough treasure interspersed around that monsters are obstacles to getting THAT THING, as opposed to just dogging you in an empty room.  I have still not seen a melee weapon swing past the normal arc, but with the amount of items and blessings around, it's possible I just haven't found one yet.  I DO know that there are blessings that allow you to make monster killing more useful, like 'each monster you kill adds 1 max hp if you smack it with this thing,' and stuff like that - tangible rewards - are what games like this should be all about. At this point, any gripes I would have about this game are mostly cosmetic nitpicking - it's nice to find developers who listen to their community, and make changes for the better on a game.  I would definitely recommend this game now, it's a fun and bouncy roguelikey dungeon delver, with achievements and perks that make the game feel different when you choose them. A+

title: Caveblazers
text: : Caveblazers is a difficult rogue-like platformer developed by Rupeck Games and published by Yogscast. You play as an adventurer that ventures into a small cave to prove a strange old man wrong, and see your way to the end of these series of caves. If you do happen to see yourself to the end of them, more plot is reviled and you get a nice little bonus of EXP. : An absolutely adorable pixel platformer. The different environment/areas are very nicely varied and each new section has a sneak preview into what the next level will be with little contaminated spots within the map. : The whole soundtrack between areas and boss fights are absolutely fantastic celtic-esque/Medieval inspired music that somehow perfectly fits the theme of the game. : Can be a little bit chunky, definitely recommend using a gamepad/controller of sorts as it makes it play much tighter and more precise. That being said, you can hate your life and use a keyboard, but this is when it begins to deteriorate in areas such as aim, can be done, just takes much more getting used to. : Let me start this off by saying, I am not a platformer fan in the slightest.. And I love this game. With the recently added local co-op, it's given it even more replay ability and entertainment which I absolutely love. With that being said, yes, it does make it even more difficult as from what I can tell, there are more enemies thrown in to compensate for the extra muscle. Maps are randomly generated which keep things interesting and keep you from memorizing where enemies, blessings or weapons may be because it changes each time you die and re-enter. The only thing that doesn't change is the fact that floors contain relics. These relics you only need to unlock once, but can do the puzzle levels as many times as you want to gain a little bonus. (Floors that contain relic puzzle spots are; 1, 3, 5, 6 and by breaking a walled-off room in the first floor of the Magma Core Area, you obtain a which you later throw into one of the Lava pools) There's a really nice amount of unlockable classes to keep things interesting and give you, the player, the option to play as anything you want to be. Be that archer, tank or wielder of magic, Caveblazers has it Another note worthy thing, this is a very skill based game that you learn as you go, there isn't a specific way to play, and it doesn't have any kind of tutorial (like the “good old days”). It has permadeath like most games similar to this do and can either be frustrating or motivating to go try again to get further than you did the time before, varies between person to person. All in all, even for someone who doesn't like styles of games such as Caveblazers, this is an exception that has granted me quite a bit of fun, especially with co-op!

title: Champions Online
text: With the fall of City of Heroes, CO is the new king of super hero MMO's. With the rising popularity of Marvel and DC movies, and the utter lack of compitition from DC online, you'd think Cryptic would have an amazing gem on there hands, right? Well sadly the answer is WRONG, Cryptic abandoned CO, if you played this game 4 years ago, you've already seen everything this game has to offer. They add some new costume packs now and then, but the main thing they keep adding to in the game is vehicles which are a total gimmick they tacked on, soley to sepperate you from your money. It is a crying shame to see the last remaining super hero MMO with an amazing character creator, left to virtually rust. Pros + The best character creator currently available, if you can think it, you can make it or close to it, not excluding any genre, from Sci Fi, to traditional caped crusaders, to super mutant furry horse monsters with bat wings and a devil tail. +Amusing combat. Not great by any means, but if you are a gold subscriber and make free form characters (potentially picking any power you want) you can make a very attractive and satisfying looking attack combo. While its a little stale at times, some powers really revolve around one or two skills, forcing you to use them over and over again, and they might look idiotic depending on your interests. + Extremely mobile travel powers! One of the best things about this game, is how fast you can move, how high you can jump, how easily you can fly. Other games will feel like your character has lead boots on, this game makes you so mobile. Cons +Dev's abandoned the game. No new dungeons/issues, no new enemies, story, anything. +Buggy as hell. These can go from game crashing to mild annoyances, either way, it magnifies the lack of Dev support. +Grindy, it used to be to easy to level up, you'd que in an instanced Alert, and kill a boss, get a big XP boost, repeat repeat repeat. However they switched it around within the last year, so the much longer, annoying robberies are the ones that give XP now. This forces you to do the missions more, and that leads to another con... +Boring missions. They are really dull, the story is so laughably neglected, they rip off of movies. Not super hero movies, sci fi movies. The villains motivations are so typical, and the quests never give you a reason to care about what your doing. +Cash shop is very price gouging. No option to unlock Free Form classes so you have to sub to play as those (Mixing power sets to make amazing combos and freedom) costume sets that they sell are really... limiting. They feel like they fit one look and one look only, opposed to CoH, which is odd since CO actually has an option to match textures.

text: I played City of Heroes for years, and this is a good echo of what was really, really good in it. Its made and modled by Cryptic so it carries many of the MMO elements from Star Trek Online, and I must admit its done right. Just suffers from a lower population limiting the economic elements. I can honestly reccomend it for people that want a good comic-hero game that isn't Marvel or DC, where you can make your own character. There are limits in the gameplay and some gripes, but for a MMO it is built solid and well. The repetitive gameplay is thankfully switched up with some slight mechanic changes. You have more direct controll over a blocking animation to redice damage for the telegraphed power attacks so it rewards timing and skill so you can face tougher opponents than just letting the character auto-attack. The mobs are also varried well with enough variety to never really make it feel like your facing the same enemies in every group as you progress. Sure there are some staples that you face repeatedly, but those are mostly cannon fodder that are there just to be beat up anyway. It makes for a good game, done well, and engaging enough to keep it going well. I would say its a great option if you want a more fun MMO that isn't too serious.

title: Champions Online
text: First the good stuff. The best character creator I've seen hands down - for any game (MMO, single player, superhero or otherwise. Just the best). Both appearance customization as well as character ability selection are out of control levels of good. The game has a charming feel to it and achieves a true comic book feel as far as how the characters act and talk as well as how the storylines progress. Lastly, the whole game is 100% free to play without spending a dime. I never felt pushed to subscribe or drop any money. Furthermore, a lot of the games extras can be unlocked through in-game currency... the catch is, it'll probably take you an absurd amount of playtime to get it so you just have to decide whether you value your money or your time more. All of that said, there are glaring downsides. The community has dwindled to a very small but dedicated few. At peak hours, it still seems fairly empty if you compare it to more popular MMOs on the market at the moment. A sizeable portion of those who are left range from largely to strictly RP fans, so not a lot of them are actually playing the game. Another big chunk are solely focused on PVP so if you're looking for help with your PVE progression, you have to dig a little. The game itself can be pretty glitchy as far as things not spawning when they should forcing you to relog to fix the problem. The system set up to guide you to objectives is patience-testing at best since that tends to glitch out as well. Sometimes objectives aren't abundantly clear and make you feel dumb after you spend 5 minutes trial and erroring a side quest. Lastly, the combat becomes a repetitive rotation of the same 2-3 powers repeatedly once you figure out what the real damage dealers/support role abilities are on your build. That may be standard RPG fare to a degree, but you sort of feel it more here due to animations being frequently recycled. Overall, definitely worth at least a few hours of your time.

title: Chroma Squad
text: It's an easy to pick up tactical RPG inspired by super sentai themed shows (aka Power Rangers, if you're in the USA). The premise is light-hearted and often lends itself to some enjoyable comedy. The balance between RPG and TV studio management at first might seem like a chore, but growing both sides turned out to be enjoyable for me. Struggling to get a leg up and gradually improving your team's costumes to get more fans to get more stuff for your studio/cast is a rewarding cycle of endeavors. I hadn't even heard of this game until I got it in a Humble Bundle with some other things I wanted. I am not disappointed so far! One thing I didn't like was that the mech battles seem to be driven by RNG in the worst possible way. 75% chance to hit = you will miss 90% of the time. Just a heads up. update: if absolutely awful final bosses are a pet peeve of yours, you should avoid this game. 99% of it is *sooo* good. And then the final boss is a teleporting enemy with the worst arena layout. Get close to attack, he teleports and then it takes your squad like 4 turns to reach him. 2 hits, then he teleports across the arena again. Instead of being strategic, it's just unnecessarily drawn out and boring. The game still gets a positive rec from me, but I don't know what the devs were thinking when they made the finale.

title: Chroma Squad
text: In a review that requires no analysis whatsoever, all you need to really know about Chroma Squad is that it feels and plays exactly like a reverent burst of childhood nostalgia. Centered around a Power Rangers motif and tactical role playing gameplay, it's a concept that is never taken too seriously and instead commits to delivering an experience both entertaining and unabashedly ridiculous. The developers clearly used an endearing sheaf of letters to spell its love for the sentai genre and consequently you'll be hard tasked to find a game executed with more fun and heart than Chroma Squad. An essential addition for anyone who wants to embrace the pure joy of video gaming.

title: Chroma Squad
text: If you haven't figured it out already, this game is essentially Power Rangers. With a bunch of comedy, hilarious dialogue, memes and 90s pop culture references thrown in for good measure. That is to say, it's a lot of fun to play, especially if you're old enough to remember the 90s. Fundamentally, the gameplay is a tactical turn based RPG. You pick your squad members at the start of the game (and use them for the entire game) and upgrade them along the way. There's no levels, you can buy new equipment and unlock new skills as you progress through the story. Unfortunately, this game is not perfect and I have a few issues with certain aspects of this game. Hopefully the devs can address some of these issues at some point. 1. Tutorial The tutorial is very light on details and skips over certain fundamental game mechanics entirely. It doesn't provide any information on what the Chromatize button does, or that you need to use it to use your finisher move. Additionally, there is very little information on what the different audience stats and numbers mean in terms of gameplay and what the different stats from the advertising agencies actually do to affect that. 2. Movement and combat Each character can generally perform two actions per turn (outside of certain free action abilities marked as such). This is fine, but the implementation is quite annoying at times. You first move action, regardless of whether you moved the full distance or not, takes up a full action. So if you moved closer to use a ranged ability and found yourself one tile too far away but still had enough movement range to do it with your first action, you have wasted the turn since to move the one additional tile will take the full second action and you will not be able to use your ranged ability. It's also hard to see where to position squad members to use abilities and teamwork without actually moving them and seeing what they can do next, compounding the frustration from the abovementioned issue. I would like to see some kind of move planner that lets you plan out all the moves for a turn (with an undo) to queue up all the actions, and when you're done setting it up, it all happens at once when you end the turn. 3. Crafting Random item drops might sound good on paper and work alright in a game with infinite random monsters to farm to eventually get what you need, but in this game it pretty much means that you'll generally be buying most of your equipment, especially since crafted items have random stats that may or may not be what you actually want/need. Save your resources for upgrading the mecha. 3. Snowballing failure Because of the story structure of this game, if you don't have the right equipment to do a mission and don't have money to afford it, you're stuck. If you do poorly on an early mission, you'll be short on cash for later missions, leading to a snowball effect of frustration with no solution other than starting over. The game is long enough that this could become rage inducing, especially given the difficulty spike at the very end. Thankfully on casual difficulty the game is easy enough that this isn't an issue at all, but could become a major problem on higher difficulties. Related to this is the major difficulty spike for the last mission, especially the final mecha battle. Tactics and equipment that worked just fine earlier in the game suddenly become useless since you're now faced with lots of new enemies and abilities. The final mecha battle has no rounds where your mech can recover, so if you didn't equip your mech with an active heal ability, you will lose, even on casual since you won't be able to heal at all, but the boss can and has a lot more health than you. Overall though I had a lot of fun playing this game in spite of my enthusiasm being dampened by the difficulty spike of the final mission. Easily recommended, especially if the devs keep working on this game and address some of the aforementioned issues.

text: Music is great. I especially enjoyed the theme. Control is very simple yet immersive. title: Chroma Squad
text: I don't think I've ever said this about a game before, but the writing makes me want to punch myself in the face. It's not bad English, it's just supernaturally bland. Banal is not a word I've ever had cause to use before, and I'm using it now. It's like... You know how five year olds write? Maybe all the words are in the right places because the teacher helped them out a bit, and maybe their spelling's all been fixed with red pen, but the story still reads like a grocery list? That's Chroma Squad. That's Chroma Squad in its excruciating, every-mission-is-a-plot-mission tedium. This would be tolerable, I guess, but the gameplay is boring too. Even on the hardest difficulty, missions just take longer to clear, and most of that time is hammering away at putties waiting for something to actually threaten you. There's a whole resource management/business sim back end to the game and that, at least, isn't boring, but it's grindy and obnoxious instead. You try to farm enough resources to craft new gear while deploying advertising bonuses to get new fans and increase revenue from viewership, while pumping your stats with a few small global bonuses, so that you can quickly and efficiently win the next mission with lots of style and max out your money gain. That's not awful, but it ends with you playing the mission, which is. If you liked Knights of Pen and Paper, you'll like this. It's a time-waster with bright colors and a surprisingly pleasant soundtrack. It has good design ideas but they're somehow lost in the implementation - like a cannoli and kidney milkshake. I tried hard to enjoy Chroma Squad, and I recognize that other people may have quite different experiences with the game, but at the end of the day, it's still just... "Once upon a time there was Teddy. He went to the store. Then he went to the beach. It rained there. The end." 0/10, Teddy. Wait a few years and try again.
